data.name: Wasps!
data.detailed_description:
NEW - now with a CHAINSAW!

Get into your garden and smash those wasps - in VR!

In Wasps! you are not the chosen one, the master of anything or born with special abilities. Forget about this!
It's your home, your garden, and you are nothing more than just anyone from the suburbs with a deep hatred for stings and buzz!

It's time to turn the tables, time to fight back and time to get those wasps out of your yard! Take your weapon and defend you property, your children and your neighborhood against those insect demons!

  • Crush as many wasps as you can!
  • Take your tools as weapons and fight off these ugly stingers!
  • Get around and find out what you may use to battle the wasps
  • Built for Steam VR and room scale gameplay

Also this game will be extended with future releases and more and more stuff is going to be added (for free), like additional weapons to use (chainsaws and flamethrowers anyone?), online leaderboards to find out who's the best wasp killer on the planet and much more.

reviews.review:
Wasps! takes one of the most irritating experiences of suburban life and turns it into an outrageous virtual reality action game. Developed and published by Mad Vulture Games, this unconventional arcade experience places players in their own backyard, where aggressive wasps have become an unbearable nuisance. Instead of assuming the role of a legendary warrior or heavily equipped soldier, players become an ordinary homeowner determined to reclaim their property through increasingly ridiculous methods of insect extermination. The premise is intentionally absurd, delivering a combination of physical combat, slapstick humor, and straightforward survival gameplay that prioritizes immediate entertainment over narrative complexity.

The central attraction is its unusual approach to combat. Rather than relying on conventional firearms, players use everyday gardening equipment and household tools to eliminate swarms of hostile insects. Weapons such as axes, lawn mowers, and chainsaws transform familiar backyard objects into instruments of destruction. This creative approach gives the game a distinctive personality, especially when combined with virtual reality motion controls. Physically swinging a weapon toward approaching enemies provides a different sensation from simply clicking a mouse button. The concept is entertaining because it exaggerates an ordinary frustration into a chaotic battle for territorial supremacy.

Its gameplay is designed around SteamVR, particularly standing and room-scale experiences associated with the HTC Vive. Players are encouraged to move around their available play area, investigate their surroundings, and discover equipment that can be used against the invading insects. This physical involvement is arguably the game's strongest feature because movement and spatial awareness become part of the challenge. Having to turn toward incoming threats or position a weapon appropriately creates a more immediate sense of participation. However, the enjoyment depends heavily on the quality of the VR equipment, motion tracking, and available physical space.

The backyard environment reinforces the game's comedic identity. Instead of transporting players into an elaborate fantasy kingdom or futuristic battlefield, the action unfolds in an ordinary residential setting. This familiar location makes the exaggerated conflict considerably more amusing. Defending a garden against flying insects is hardly an epic adventure, yet the game treats the situation with enough exaggerated aggression to create its own entertaining atmosphere. Unfortunately, the relatively restricted environment also suggests limited opportunities for meaningful exploration. Players seeking elaborate locations, environmental storytelling, or substantial world-building will find the concept considerably narrower than traditional action adventures.

The combat system emphasizes accessibility and instant gratification rather than tactical sophistication. Its basic objective of destroying as many wasps as possible is easy to understand, making the experience approachable for players who simply want to enjoy a few rounds of virtual reality mayhem. Experimenting with different tools offers some variety, particularly when switching between conventional gardening implements and more destructive equipment. Nevertheless, the straightforward premise raises concerns about repetition. Without extensive enemy variety, complicated objectives, or a meaningful progression system, the central activity risks becoming predictable after the initial novelty disappears.

Another interesting element is the game's achievement system, which includes 32 Steam achievements. These provide additional objectives for players who enjoy completion challenges and can offer motivation beyond simply eliminating insects. Achievement hunting may extend the experience for dedicated players, although collecting rewards does not necessarily compensate for limited mechanical depth. The developers also discussed expanding the experience through additional weapons, competitive leaderboards, and other content. However, those earlier ambitions should not be confused with verified features of the current version.

Visually, the game appears more concerned with functional VR interaction and its unusual setting than with delivering an elaborate graphical spectacle. Its relatively modest installation size reflects its compact design, although storage requirements alone cannot determine graphical quality. The appeal primarily comes from seeing ordinary gardening equipment become part of an exaggerated insect battle. Audio could also contribute to the atmosphere, particularly through the unsettling presence of buzzing insects and the impact of improvised weapons. However, the available information does not establish whether its sound design or visual effects offer exceptional technical polish.

Accessibility presents another significant limitation. The game supports single-player gameplay, tracked motion controllers, and English and German language options, but it is exclusively designed for virtual reality. Consequently, players cannot expect a conventional desktop experience using only a keyboard and mouse. Its physical nature may also make it unsuitable for individuals with restricted movement or insufficient room space. These requirements considerably narrow its potential audience, even though the underlying gameplay concept is uncomplicated.

Steam Deck compatibility is officially listed as Unknown. More importantly, the game requires a VR headset and compatible motion-tracking equipment, meaning it cannot be played normally using the Steam Deck's integrated screen and controls. It should therefore be considered unsuitable for standard handheld gameplay. Anyone hoping to experience it on Valve's portable device without specialized external equipment should look elsewhere.

Ultimately, Wasps! succeeds more as an amusing virtual reality experiment than as a substantial action game. Its greatest appeal lies in transforming an everyday annoyance into a ridiculous backyard battle, supported by unconventional weapons and physically interactive gameplay. However, the narrow setting, potentially repetitive combat, limited apparent progression, and mandatory VR equipment prevent it from becoming an easy recommendation. It may provide some entertaining moments for VR enthusiasts who appreciate strange arcade concepts, but players expecting extensive content or sophisticated mechanics should manage their expectations.

The game deserves recognition for its humorous premise and inventive use of household tools, but its limited scope and specialized hardware requirements considerably restrict its lasting appeal. It is a curious diversion for dedicated VR players rather than an essential addition to an action game collection.

Rating: 5/10
